subject: Post-call recap: ACME technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs, deployment topology)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs, deployment topology)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and the proposed next steps to keep momentum for the technical deep-dive: 

Pain points you called out
- p95 latency spikes on concurrent chat sessions impacting UX during peak (Black Friday-like loads).
- Need predictable throughput for a bursty inference workload (concurrent live users + background batch reranks).
- Tight cost targets for inference unit economics while preserving quality on a 65B-ish chat model.
- Data residency requirement for US-only deployment and auditability (retention & audit logs).

Goals you shared
- P95 response target: ~150-300ms depending on prompt length; firm SLA target of 99.95% availability for inference endpoints.
- Support 300-600 concurrent interactive sessions with average prompt length ~200 tokens and occasional long-form generation (~2k tokens) for summaries.
- Keep incremental per-token spend within project budget (we discussed goal to < $0.002/token produced but understand this is adjustable after sizing).

Summary of what we discussed technically
- Model: you prefer an open-chat capable model (we discussed Llama2-chat / open 65B variants) with quantization for cost.
- Topology: likely Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in us-west region with autoscaling headroom and a fallback to hosted lower-cost variant for overflow.
- Optimizations: KV-prefix caching for repeated context, request-aware batching, and routing policies that prefer low-latency nodes for interactive sessions.

Attachments: I attached a short write-up and a draft deployment topology diagram to start the TD prep.
- 20260215-acme-td-summary.pdf (summary + SLO table)
- acme-deployment-topology-draft.png

Proposed next steps
1) Schedule a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive the week of Feb 22: include your infra + platform engineers, our runtime/serving engineer (Dev Patel), and our SRE/architecture lead if possible.
2) Share any internal perf benchmarks or traffic p95/p99 histograms ahead of the meeting (helps us size batching/queueing).
3) We’ll come prepared with: latency/throughput estimates for the 65B quantized path, fallback topology options, and a first-pass SLO table for your review.

Can you confirm availability for Feb 23–25 (US time)? If you prefer a specific agenda or additional attendees, let me know and I’ll include them.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs, deployment topology)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the TD is focused: 
- The 150–300ms p95 is our target for short prompts (~<=512 tokens). For long-form jobs (~2k tokens) we expect relaxed latency and can accept p95 up to ~800ms for generation, but p99 should still remain reasonable.
- Our burst profile: baseline concurrent interactive sessions ~300, peak bursts up to ~600 for sales events.
- Availability target is accurate (99.95%). For cost target, the team would like to aim for <= $0.002/token produced for normal traffic — if your sizing shows that’s infeasible for 65B we’re open to discussing a 30–40% cheaper fallback model for overflow.
- Data residency: all production inference must be in US regions and logs retained per our policy.

We can do Feb 24, 10:00–11:30 PT for the TD. That should give us time to include two infra engineers and our platform lead. Please send an invite and any pre-read.

Quick question: do you have an internal SLO template we can review to align expectations?

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, ACME Inc.
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
